evidence: flushPausedPanes fires each Continue fire-and-forget (`void ... .catch`) and then calls `pausedPanes.clear()` in the same tick, so no maybeResume can run between a fired Continue and the clear, and afterwards maybeResume returns on `flow === undefined`. The flag the reviewer wanted set would sit on an object that is dropped right away.

The fallthrough `err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown error"` threw away all information about a non-Error rejection. 2cbe346 replaces it with `non-Error rejection (${typeof err})`, and `typeof` cannot throw.
guidance_note: When a total error mapper avoids String() for safety, keep a cheap discriminator such as typeof in the fallback instead of a constant placeholder.

Vitest's hang detection tracks timers and I/O, and a pending promise with no timer or I/O behind it is not one; nothing in the packet shows a flagged handle or a leak. The deferred rewrite in 5ab1d6d is harmless churn on an overstated premise.

narrative: This is a decomposition of bridge-connection.ts into two ledgers. Most findings in later rounds are gaps in the original extraction that the reviewer surfaced one round at a time, not defects from fixes. All ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags except F15 are false positives on pre-existing code. The costly call was deferring the confirmed releasePeer phantom race (F5/F6): the agent claimed it needed async teardown, then fixed it locally one round later when the reviewer re-raised it (F10/F11). The only fix-caused finding is F15, whose premise about a dangling promise was overstated.
guidance_observations: A confirmed bug was deferred on a guessed fix cost; spiking the fix (or writing the failing test) first would have shown it was local and saved two repeat threads.
The reviewer found new pre-existing coverage gaps every round; one full coverage pass over the extracted classes before the first push would have collapsed rounds 2-4.
The agent pushed back correctly on F1 by reading the synchronous fire-then-clear control flow, and correctly reshaped F9 and F13 instead of applying the reviewer's literal fix.

evidence: bufferSeed/bufferWrite only documented the `buffering` precondition. Calling them after the gate opened would leave content in fields nothing drains. 60d866d adds `assertBuffering` (a throw) plus three tests, and the agent rejected the heavier BufferingGate type split on carrying-cost grounds.
guidance_note: When a new class's method documents a phase precondition, enforce it in the method in the original PR instead of relying on the single caller's guard.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 from a second scope. The same 60d866d assert-or-throw fix covers it, which was the reviewer's first option.

The flag is a false positive: 60d866d appended new precondition tests, and the `toBe(a)` identity assertions were in the original test file. The gate is off the hot path, so forwarding by reference is not its contract; b02fe48 drops the identity checks and keeps `toEqual([a, b])`.
guidance_note: Assert identity in tests only when zero-copy is a documented contract of the unit under test.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 60d866d did not touch index.ts, and the agent says the flag-before-resize order predates the split. `firstResizeDone = true` ran before `terminal.resize()`, so a throw would leave the machine past first resize while the gate still buffered. b02fe48 moves the assignment after the resize.
guidance_note: Advance a phase flag only after the operation it names has succeeded, even when moving existing code verbatim.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: b02fe48 only moved the firstResizeDone assignment inside the rAF callback and did not touch the constructor's open-then-VisibilityTracker order, which came from the original split. IntersectionObserver callbacks are asynchronous and observe the container's own box, so line order has no correctness effect. Observing xterm's internal element would couple the tracker to xterm internals.

narrative: This is a clean split of xterm-sink into a gate, a tracker and a bytes sink. Round 0 raised one real precondition hole, twice; it was fixed with a loud assert. Every ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag in rounds 1-2 points at code from the original split or an earlier order, not at the fix commits, so no finding was caused by a fix. The agent accepted the two valid hardening findings and correctly pushed back on the IntersectionObserver ordering claim.
guidance_observations: Each follow-up round raised pre-existing issues rather than defects from fixes, so the extra rounds came from the reviewer's incremental coverage, not bad fixes.
The agent chose the lighter of the reviewer's two options for F1/F2 (assert vs type split) and argued it on carrying cost.
